title: PG-W-21D Device pairing and recovery: a one-tap signed act pairs a new device at low trust, and a lost device is recovered through the owner's recovery key or an operator re-grant (memev)
request: Contract PG-W-21D in memev: device pairing and recovery under ADR 8 (trust governance), work package WP21-D1. Unsigned: a spec proposed for red-team review. ORIGIN. The owner answered ADR 8 on 1 Nov 2026. Question 3: the owner's new device has low trust, raised by a one-tap from a trusted device, else zero. Clarification 1: no trust record in personal scope; low trust means contribute-only at required verification 1, in the owner's organisational scopes only, never above the owner. Clarification 2: the one-tap is the person's signed act and records the approving device; a lost device is recovered through the owner's recovery key or an operator re-grant. This contract builds that act and that recovery as one new module and changes no existing one. WHAT IT BUILDS. (1) src/engine/federation/pairing.mjs: a pairing request from the new device (its subject id, its Ed25519 public key, its owner, the one-time invite it redeemed); a deterministic low-trust derivation from the owner's identity document (purposes exactly contribute, required verification 1, scopes only the organisational scopes where the owner holds a live membership, an expiry no later than any of those memberships and no later than 90 days); a one-tap approval, which is the person's signature, in the namespace memev-pairing, over the request hash, the scopes, the approving device and a short expiry; the check of that approval; and pairDevice, which redeems the invite and enrols the computer through the existing code of src/engine/devices.mjs (redeemInvite, DeviceRegistry.enroll, with its seat policy unchanged), appends audit events to the operation log and hands the derived grant proposal to the trust book of PG-W-21B. (2) Recovery: a person's recovery key, a key of the person subject whose id is recovery or starts with recovery-, signs the same approval for the same low trust without any trusted device; an operator re-grant is the same approval signed by an operator subject of the organisation scope, limited to that scope; losing a device revokes it through DeviceRegistry.revoke and asks the trust book to revoke what it was granted. WHAT IT REUSES AND DOES NOT CHANGE. src/engine/identity.mjs (subject, scope and membership validation, resolveActor, isResolvedActor) and src/engine/devices.mjs (the registry, the invite, the device key and its proof) are reused unchanged: the contract adds no second identity model and no second device registry. The trusted device is the vault host (the registry device of kind host); a paired device is low trust and can approve nothing, so there is no chain. Enrolment alone (redeemInvite as today) gives a device no trust record: that is the zero of Question 3. Personal vault sync for a device goes on through its existing token and seat and is not a trust record. BOUNDARIES. (a) The trust record format (signature block, required verification level, reserved delegation, root records with succession, the personal-scope rule) is PG-W-21A.2 and the book that writes and revokes grants (only a person or operator, signed and logged, GRANT_AUTHORITY provisional under ADR 5) is the amended PG-W-21B; both are cited by id and not repeated. This contract hands the book a grant proposal { subject, scopes, purposes, required_verification, expires } and a resolved actor, and the book writes the record in the format of PG-W-21A.2. The book interface used here (grant and revoke with a resolved actor) is the one of PG-W-21B and is aligned with its amendment before signing. (b) Revocation notices and their push are not here (PG-W-21C and PG-W-21G belong to another author). (c) Entitlement is not here: pairing your own devices is local trust and free; seats stay the existing seat policy (Free: this computer; Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers; Business and Corporate by contacting us); PG-W-21E gates multi-site and cross-organisation use. (d) The topology of work breakdown row 1.3.6 stays OPEN; ADR 3, ADR 5, ADR 7 and SO-A-05 stay open and nothing here decides them; raising a device above low trust is not a pairing act and is an ordinary grant of the trust book. Depends on contracts: PG-W-21A.2 (unsigned, proposed in parallel), SO-F-01 (built), and the amended PG-W-21B for the book. Base revision: 4db303071c67c32e2e5b3ecd508a10748b5b5a34, the memev main commit this spec was written against and the commit the red runs are judged at. The tests reach the module by namespace import() inside each test with typeof asserts, so a missing export fails on an assertion and not at load. Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository; tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that; there is no Federated tier.

tasks.title: A new device is paired at low trust by a one-tap signed act of the person, from the trusted device, and has no trust until then
requirements: src/engine/federation/pairing.mjs (new) exports PAIRING_NAMESPACE (memev-pairing), REQUEST_SCHEMA (memev-pairing-request/1), APPROVAL_SCHEMA (memev-pairing-approval/1), LOW_TRUST (frozen: purposes ['contribute'], required_verification 1), APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS (900), DEVICE_GRANT_MAX_DAYS (90), requestPairing, requestHash, deriveLowTrust, approvePairing, verifyApproval and pairDevice; no function throws on bad input, each returns { ok: false, code, reason } instead

requestPairing validates the device subject id (a device subject of src/engine/identity.mjs, through validateSubject), the owner (a person subject), the device public key (through publicKeyFrom of src/engine/devices.mjs, so only an Ed25519 key passes) and the invite id; requestHash is the SHA-256 of the canonical text of the request and is the same for equal requests (source: validateSubject in src/engine/identity.mjs, publicKeyFrom in src/engine/devices.mjs)

deriveLowTrust({ request, identity, scopes, at, days }) is pure: the grantable scopes are the scopes of the identity document that are not personal and where the owner has a membership that is live at the time; a requested scope outside them (a personal scope, a scope the owner has no live membership in) is refused with above_owner; with none requested all of them are taken; purposes are exactly contribute, the required verification is exactly 1, the expiry is the earliest of the time plus days (at most DEVICE_GRANT_MAX_DAYS), and the expiry of each membership used; an owner who is revoked or expired gets a refusal; an owner with only a personal scope gets an ok result with no scopes, which is zero trust (source: authorizeScope and validateMembership in src/engine/identity.mjs; PG-W-21A.2 personal-scope rule)

approvePairing makes the approval { schema, request_hash, person, approved_device, via 'one_tap', scopes, approved_at, expires_at, signature } and signs it with the person's key through a sign function the caller gives (signNamespaced of src/engine/agentid-bind.mjs in the namespace memev-pairing); verifyApproval checks, with a replaceable verifier, that the person is the owner of the request, that the signature verifies with a live key of that person in the identity document, that request_hash is the hash of the request given, that the approval has not expired, that the scopes are within deriveLowTrust, and that approved_device is the trusted device; a changed field, another request, another person's key, an agent, service or device key, an expired approval and a paired low-trust device as approver are each refused with their own code

the trusted device is the vault host: the registry device of kind host and status active, owned by the same person; a device that was itself paired has low trust and approves nothing, so there is no chain of approvals (decision for the red-team: an owner-designated trusted device is the alternative and is not built here)

pairDevice({ root, tokens, code, request, approval, identity, log, book, actor, at, verify, policy }) refuses a pairing with no approval (nothing is enrolled and nothing is logged), then redeems the invite and enrols the computer through redeemInvite and DeviceRegistry.enroll of src/engine/devices.mjs, which keep their one-time, expiry and seat rules (a full seat policy refuses with the code seats and leaves nothing logged and no grant); an approval is single use, which the log shows; after enrolment it appends federation.pairing.approved to the operation log with the request hash, the device, the person, the approving device, the scopes, the purposes, the level and the expiry, and no invite secret, token, private key or public key; it then calls book.grant once for each scope with the proposal and the resolved actor of the person (isResolvedActor of src/engine/identity.mjs), never for a personal scope; a book that refuses leaves the device enrolled with no trust and appends federation.pairing.refused with the code

enrolment alone (redeemInvite as it is today) records no pairing event and gives no grant: the device has zero trust until a pairing approval is made; a paired device keeps using its existing token, scope and seat for the personal vault, which is not a trust record

src/engine/identity.mjs, src/engine/devices.mjs, src/engine/entitlements.mjs, src/engine/license.mjs and every other file of src/engine/federation are not changed; pairing.mjs imports identity.mjs, devices.mjs and agentid-bind.mjs and defines no identity model, no device registry and no key parser of its own; each red-green criterion runs only its own subtest whose name starts with T1-cNN: (source: the convention of SR-0.03.3 T1 requirement 8)
tasks.description: Repo: memev. The fixtures are an identity document with a person, a host device, a new device, an operator and two scopes (one organisational scope with a live membership, one personal), a DeviceRegistry and TokenStore in a temporary directory, a vault OpLog, a fake trust book { grant, revoke } that records its calls, and a fake sign and verify pair that hashes the signed message so a test sees what a signature covers, with one real ssh-keygen round trip. A stand-in of every subtest was run read-only at the base: each fails on ERR_ASSERTION, none on a load error or a TypeError.

tasks.title: A lost device is revoked, and a replacement is paired through the owner's recovery key or an operator re-grant at the same low trust
requirements: recoveryKeyOf(identity, person) returns the live keys of the person subject whose id is recovery or starts with recovery- (a naming convention, because the key schema of src/engine/identity.mjs has no use field and is not changed); approveWithRecoveryKey makes the approval of T1 with via recovery_key and approved_device null, signed with a recovery key, for the same low trust and no more; verifyApproval accepts it with no trusted device present, and refuses a recovery key that is revoked or expired, an ordinary key of the person on this path, a recovery key on the one_tap path, and any key of another person

approveAsOperator makes the approval of T1 with via operator, signed by a subject of type operator that has a live membership in every scope it grants; the scopes are limited to the scopes of that operator that the owner is also a member of; a personal scope, a scope outside the operator's membership, and a signer that is a person, agent, service, device or node are refused; the result is the same low trust of T1 and nothing higher

no recovery path raises trust: every approval, whatever its via, derives exactly LOW_TRUST (purposes contribute, required verification 1) within the owner's organisational scopes and no more; an approval of any via is single use and expires after APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS; raising a device above low trust is an ordinary grant of the trust book (PG-W-21B) and not a pairing act

revokeDevice({ registry, tokens, deviceId, by, reason, log, book, actor, at }) revokes the device through DeviceRegistry.revoke of src/engine/devices.mjs (its token stops and its seat is free), appends federation.pairing.revoked with the device, who revoked it and the reason, and calls book.revoke once for each scope the log shows was granted to the device, with the reason; the reason is one of compromised, left and error and defaults to compromised (the marking of earlier work from a revoked source is the overlay of PG-W-21B and is not built here); the host device and an unknown device are refused; a book that refuses is reported and does not undo the device revocation

pairDevice of T1 accepts an approval of any of the three vias and pairs the replacement the same way; recovery paths are logged with their via in federation.pairing.approved and add no other event type; the new device of a recovery is paired through a new invite, never through the credentials of the lost one

docs/IDENTITY-AND-SCOPES.md describes the recovery key convention, the operator re-grant, the revocation of a lost device and that none of them raises trust; the files of T1 stay as they are apart from pairing.mjs, its test, the docs and the module map; each red-green criterion runs only its own subtest whose name starts with T2-cNN:
tasks.description: Repo: memev. Builds on T1 and uses its fixtures, with a recovery key and an ordinary key on the person subject, an operator subject with a membership in one of two organisational scopes, and a lost device that was paired earlier. A stand-in of every subtest was run read-only at the base: each fails on ERR_ASSERTION.

stop_rules: No weakening of an existing test, no raised timeout, no skip, no widened scope; if blocked, report what blocks and continue with the next independent task.
A criterion that cannot be checked from this repository is reported as unchecked, never marked as passing.
Anything outside the requirements of this task is not built, not stubbed and not defaulted in code; if the work seems to need it, stop and report what it needs.
A test_red_green command of this contract prints its whole output: it is never piped through tail or head, and never captures its output without printing it.

Stop and ask when the work would decide ADR 3, ADR 5, ADR 7 or SO-A-05, add a role-by-action matrix, pick the topology of work breakdown row 1.3.6, or touch the licence terms, the tier prices or the crdt-merge terms.
Stop and ask when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would edit a signed spec or a signed contract: a signed id is superseded by a new id, never edited.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
Stop and ask when the work would change the key schema of src/engine/identity.mjs to mark a recovery key, or when a recovery path would grant more than low trust.
